title: Contacts
summary: The people at a customer. Who gets emailed, who can log in, and how to move a contact to a different customer.
html:
A customer is a company; a contact is a person at it. Quotes and invoices are addressed to a customer, but they are emailed to a contact, so a customer with no contacts cannot be sent anything.

Adding a contact

Open the customer and use Add Contact. A contact needs a first name and an email address. Everything else — phone numbers, job title, a second address — is optional.

One contact per customer is marked as the primary contact. That is the one that gets used by default when you email a quote or an invoice, and the one shown in list screens.

Letting a contact log in

A contact can be given a password and allowed into the customer portal, where they see their own quotes, invoices, tickets and files. Set this up on the contact record itself: give them a login and a password, and make sure the customer portal is switched on in Settings.

See The customer portal for what they can do once they are in.

A contact who cannot reset their password is usually a contact with no email address saved, or an installation that cannot send mail at all — check Troubleshooting before assuming the login is broken.

Moving a contact to another customer

Contacts are attached to one customer at a time. To move one, edit the contact and change the customer it belongs to. History attached to the contact — tickets they raised, emails sent to them — moves with them.

This is the usual fix when the same person is entered twice under two companies. Move one, then delete the duplicate.
